BLM’S REQUEST TO VACATE AND REMAND DECISION DENIED
On November 9, 2005, counsel of record for the Bureau of Land Management (BLM)
filed the Bureau Of Land Management’s Request To Vacate And Remand Decision. On
November 15, 2005, the undersigned issued an Order affording the Appellants and the
Intervenors until November 23, 2005, in which to file a response to said request. In turn, on
November 21, 2005, counsel of record for the Appellants filed Appellants’ Opposition To BLM’s
Motion To Vacate And Remand.
BLM’s request is premised, in part, upon the content of the Order issued by the
undersigned on July 5, 2005, which included a partial stay of the April 22, 2005, Final Decision
on appeal herein. My July 5th Order stayed only a portion of BLM’s Decision on appeal, namely,
that portion of the Decision, which authorized certain range improvement projects. My July 5th
Order did not stay the grazing system portion of BLM’s Final Decision.
BLM’s instant request to vacate, raises the procedurally interesting issue of whether or
not the Appellants are procedurally entitled to appeal and adjudicate that portion of BLM’s
Decision which was not stayed in my July 5th Order, or whether, in the alternative, BLM is
somehow automatically entitled to vacate the totality of the Bureau’s formally issued Decision,
under circumstances where the grazing portion of that Decision was not stayed. Stated somewhat
differently the issue is as follows: As a matter of procedural due process, does BLM enjoy a
unilateral, procedural right to vacate its Decision in toto, or, in the alternative, do the Appellants
and Intervenors enjoy the jurisdictional right to have the grazing portion of BLM’s Decision fully
adjudicated on the record.
Because my July 5th Order stayed only a portion of BLM’s Decision on appeal herein, the
Appellants and Intervenors enjoy a jurisdictional, procedural right to appeal and have fully
adjudicated, in an APA on-the-record hearing, the grazing portion of BLM’s Decision, which has
4

not been stayed. Under the provisions of 43 C.F.R. 4.472 (e), “Any final BLM grazing decision
that is not already in effect and for which a stay is not granted will become effective immediately
after the administrative law judge denies a petition for a stay ... .” I denied the petition for stay
with respect to the grazing portion of BLM’s Final Decision, which, therefore, became “effective
immediately.” In my Order dated October 21, 2005, which denied BLM’s earlier request for
remand in this matter, I stated the following, “Another, potential procedural avenue would be a
Motion To Vacate and Remand by BLM, which would require the concurrence of the Appellants
and Intervenors.” (Emphasis added; Order-- “BLM’s Request For Remand Denied,” October 21,
2005, p. 5). I reiterate strongly my view that for the government to vacate this docket, the
concurrence of the other parties in interest is procedurally required, because the grazing portion
of BLM’s decision is in effect under the referenced regulatory provision.
Relatedly, as a procedural matter, “Any applicant, permittee, lessee, or other person
whose interest is adversely affected by a final BLM grazing decision may appeal the decision to
an administrative law judge ... .” 43 C.F.R. 4.470. Having timely filed their original appeal, the
Appellants have a jurisdictional, procedural right to adjudicate the grazing portion of BLM’s
Decision, and BLM does not enjoy any unilateral, procedural right to subvert the appellate rights
of the Appellants through an untimely motion to vacate. Jurisdiction over BLM’s Final Decision
on appeal reposes exclusively in the Departmental Cases Hearings Division.
In this context, as Appellants correctly point out in their Opposition, BLM has known of
the scheduled hearing for months. Indeed, the hearing in this matter was the subject of a
telephone conference conducted by the undersigned on July 26, 2005, which included Kenneth
M. Sebby, Esq., on behalf of BLM; Todd C. Tucci, Esq., on behalf of the Appellants; Richard
and Connie Brandau, Intervenors; and William Watterson, Intervenor. During that conference,
the undersigned, the BLM, the Appellants, and each of the Intervenors specifically agreed to
commence the public hearing on December 12, 2005, and, if not completed, to reconvene the
hearing on January 23, 2006. The government cannot claim lack of advance notice with respect
to the scheduled hearing.
For the above-stated jurisdictional and procedural reasons, BLM’s Request To Vacate
And Remand Decision is DENIED. The public hearing in this matter will commence at 1:00
p.m. on Monday, December 12, 2005, in Caldwell, Idaho, at the place designated in the Owyhee
Field Manager’s Notice dated November 1, 2005.
James H. Heffernan
Administrative Law Judge
